The distortion product otoacoustic emissions (DP-OAE) test is useful in monitoring cisplatin-induced ototoxicity in children. Evidence indicates that high-frequency hearing loss is common in children undergoing cisplatin treatment, with significant deterioration observed post-therapy, particularly in those without spontaneous otoacoustic emissions prior to treatment [2]. The DP-OAE test can detect changes in cochlear function, as shown in studies where reductions in DP-OAE were noted alongside threshold changes in extended high-frequency pure-tone audiometry [1]. This suggests that DP-OAE is a valuable tool for early detection of ototoxicity, allowing for timely interventions to manage hearing loss in pediatric patients receiving cisplatin [1][2].

Therefore, changes in QRS and T vectors post-CRT are relevant indicators of survival in this patient population.
